title: Maximum Number of Removable Characters
prompt: You are given two strings `s` and `p` where `p` is a subsequence of `s`, and an array `removable` containing distinct indices of `s` that can be removed, listed in the order they should be removed. Find the maximum value `k` (0 <= k <= removable.length) such that after removing the first `k` characters from `s` (using the indices in `removable`), `p` is still a subsequence of the resulting string `s`. Return that maximum `k`.

examples.explanation: After removing the characters at indices 3 and 1, s becomes "accb", and "ab" is still a subsequence. Removing the character at index 0 as well would eliminate the required 'a'.
With repeated characters, up to 2 of the 3 a's can be removed and "a" is still a subsequence of what's left.

constraints: removable.length == length of a subset of distinct indices of s
p is a subsequence of s
hints: Checking each prefix length k from 0 upward and verifying whether p is still a subsequence after removing those k characters would work, but you can do better than testing every k one at a time.

Whether p remains a subsequence after removing the first k indices from removable is a monotonic property: if it fails for some k, it fails for every larger k too, since more characters have been removed.
Binary search on k itself over the range [0, removable.length], using a standard O(n) subsequence check as the feasibility test at each candidate k.

solution.approach: The feasibility of p remaining a subsequence after removing the first k characters (by removable order) is monotonic in k: removing more characters can only make it harder, never easier, for p to still be a subsequence. This means binary search applies directly to k. For a candidate k, mark the first k indices from removable as deleted, then run a standard two-pointer subsequence check between s (skipping deleted positions) and p in O(n) time. Binary searching over k with this check gives an O(n log(removable.length)) solution overall.
